chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz, from Ayub ibn Nuh and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father (all of them), from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Sunnah divorce is when he divorces her with one pronouncement, meaning during a period of purity from non-consummation, with the testimony of two witnesses. Then he leaves her until her menstrual periods pass. When her menstrual periods have passed, she is definitively divorced from him, and he is a suitor among suitors; if she wishes, she may marry him, and if she wishes, she may not.
And if he wishes to take her back, he should witness her return before her menstrual periods pass, so she remains with him under the previous pronouncement.
He said, and Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'This is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [them] in an acceptable manner or release [them] with good treatment.
The third pronouncement is releasing [her] with good treatment.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She is definitively divorced from him
key_terms.بِشَهَادَةِ شَاهِدَيْنِ: With the testimony of two witnesses
key_terms.طَلاَقُ السُّنَّةِ: Sunnah divorce (divorce following the Prophet's method)
key_terms.عَلَى طُهْرٍ: During a period of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for Sunnah divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the procedural mechanics of *Talaq al-Sunnah*, emphasizing the specific condition of pronouncing a single divorce during a period of purity (*Tuhr*) free from intercourse, as narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It clarifies that if the husband revokes the divorce before the three menstrual cycles conclude, the marriage remains under the original ruling; however, once the *Iddah* expires, the divorce becomes final (*Bain*), requiring a new contract for remarriage. The text explicitly links this practice to the Quranic verse 2:229, categorizing the third and final release as 'sending away with kindness' (*Tasreeh bi-Ihsan*).
